description:
lib.rs:1577-1582 (run_chain) calls run_cert per cert position, and run_cert (lib.rs:1494) calls cert_sha256_of(cert) once per call. If a caller's chain contains the same Certificate at multiple positions (e.g. a self-signed CA tested at both Leaf and AnchorIssued positions for shape tests, as in the lib.rs tests at line 2126-2134), the hash is recomputed each time.

Hashing a DER-encoded cert is a few microseconds — negligible for short chains. Becomes meaningful for batch evidence-pack runs where the same trust anchor appears at the top of every chain.

Fix shape: a SHA-256 cache keyed on a cheap cert identity. The cheapest identity is &Certificate as a pointer-equality key (rejects clones but matches the test pattern of cert.clone() at multiple positions). Or: hash on first encounter and stuff the result into a Vec<Option<[u8;32]>> parallel to chain[].

Not P0 — current performance is dominated by signature verification in real chains, not hashing. Worth a follow-up bead so the hot path is visible if it becomes hot.
title: run_chain rehashes the same cert at each chain position
